Blood fats respond to diet, activity and weight; ask your doctor whether more is needed.
Drink enough water unless told otherwise, and review painkillers and other medicines with your doctor.
Limit alcohol and fatty food, and tell your doctor about all medicines and supplements.
Thyroid levels change slowly; your doctor may want to re-check or adjust treatment.
Blood counts change with diet, iron, infections and medicines; discuss this with your doctor.
Sunlight, food and supplements affect vitamin levels; ask your doctor about the right dose.
Less salt, daily activity, good sleep and calm help blood pressure; measure at the same time each day.
Small daily habits such as portions, walking and sleep make the biggest difference to weight.
